text: Which of the following molecules contains carbon-carbon bonds with the most s-character?
explainAnswer: Identify the hybridization of the carbon atoms in each molecule.
Determine the s-character associated with each type of hybridization: sp has 50% s-character, sp2 has 33% s-character, and sp3 has 25% s-character.
Compare the s-character of the carbon-carbon bonds in each molecule based on their hybridization.
Conclude that ethyne, with sp hybridization, has the most s-character in its carbon-carbon bonds.

text: When cobalt (III) ions react with ammonia, they form an octahedral coordination compound. What is the chemical formula and charge of this compound?
explainAnswer: Identify the oxidation state of cobalt in the compound, which is +3 for cobalt (III).
Recognize that ammonia (NH3) acts as a neutral ligand and does not contribute any charge.
Determine the coordination number for cobalt in an octahedral complex, which is typically 6.
Write the formula by combining the cobalt ion with the ammonia ligands, resulting in Co(NH3)6.
Since cobalt has a +3 charge and ammonia is neutral, the overall charge of the compound is +3.

text: What is the term for a 50/50 mixture of enantiomers?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of enantiomers as molecules that are mirror images of each other.
Understand that a 50/50 mixture means there are equal amounts of both enantiomers present.
Recognize that a mixture containing equal amounts of both enantiomers is referred to as a racemic mixture.
Conclude that the term for a 50/50 mixture of enantiomers is racemic mixture.

text: Nick has an unknown compound that he has determined to be soluble in water and produces a solution that is not electrically conductive. Which of the following might the compound be?
explainAnswer: Identify that the compound is soluble in water.
Determine that a solution that is not electrically conductive suggests the compound does not dissociate into ions.
Evaluate the choices: Sodium chloride dissociates into ions and conducts electricity, Silicon dioxide is not soluble in water, and Hexane is not soluble in water.
Conclude that Sucrose is soluble in water and does not produce ions, making it the correct choice.

text: Neon has an atomic mass of 20.19 amu. Which of the following explains why this is?
choices: Each atom of neon has a mass of 20.19 amu
Neon likely has a true atomic mass of 20 amu, but mass spectrometry is not precise enough to determine its exact mass
Neon can have a variable number of protons and therefore a range of masses
Neon has three naturally abundant isotopes, but the most common is neon-20
explainAnswer: Identify that atomic mass is a weighted average of all isotopes of an element.
Recognize that neon has multiple isotopes, specifically neon-20, neon-21, and neon-22.
Understand that the atomic mass of 20.19 amu reflects the relative abundances of these isotopes.
Conclude that the presence of isotopes, particularly the most abundant one, influences the average atomic mass.

text: Based on their bond-dissociation energies, which of the following bonds is strongest?
explainAnswer: Identify the bond-dissociation energies for each bond type listed in the choices.
Compare the bond-dissociation energies to determine which bond requires the most energy to break.
The bond with the highest bond-dissociation energy is the strongest bond.
Select the bond that has the highest energy value from your comparison, which in this case is N triple bond N.

text: What rule states that electrons will half-fill orbitals before pairing up?
explainAnswer: Identify the context of electron configuration in atomic theory.
Understand the principles of orbital filling and the order in which electrons occupy orbitals.
Recall that electrons will occupy empty orbitals singly before pairing up in the same orbital.
Recognize that this principle is known as Hund's Rule.

text: Rank the following three molecules in terms of increasing volatility: 1) Butanoic [byoo-tan-OH-ik] acid; 2) Butanal [byoo-ta-NAL]; 3) Butane.
explainAnswer: Identify the functional groups present in each molecule: Butanoic acid has a carboxylic acid group, Butanal has an aldehyde group, and Butane is an alkane.

Determine the strength of intermolecular forces for each molecule: Carboxylic acids have strong hydrogen bonding, aldehydes have moderate dipole-dipole interactions, and alkanes have weak London dispersion forces.
Rank the molecules based on the strength of their intermolecular forces: stronger forces lead to lower volatility.
Conclude that Butanoic acid is the least volatile, followed by Butanal, and Butane is the most volatile.

text: What is the chemical formula of ethanamine [eth-AN-ah-meen]?
explainAnswer: Identify that ethanamine is an amine derived from ethane.
Determine the structure of ethane, which is C2H6.
Replace one hydrogen atom in ethane with an amino group (-NH2) to form ethanamine.
Write the chemical formula by counting the remaining hydrogen atoms and the amino group, resulting in C2H7N.

text: What is the oxidation state of chromium in K<sub>2</sub>Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub>?
explainAnswer: Identify the oxidation states of the other elements in the compound: potassium (K) is +1 and oxygen (O) is -2.
Since there are two potassium atoms, their total contribution is +2.
There are seven oxygen atoms, contributing a total of -14.
Let x be the oxidation state of chromium (Cr); set up the equation: 2 + 2x - 14 = 0.
Solve for x to find that x = +6.

text: Identify all of the following three factors that can affect the rate of a chemical reaction: 1) Changing the temperature; 2) Changing the concentration of the reactants; 3) Adding a catalyst.
explainAnswer: Recognize that the rate of a chemical reaction can be influenced by various factors.
Identify the three factors listed: temperature, concentration of reactants, and presence of a catalyst.
Understand that increasing temperature generally increases reaction rates due to higher kinetic energy.
Realize that increasing the concentration of reactants typically leads to more frequent collisions, thus increasing the reaction rate.
Acknowledge that adding a catalyst lowers the activation energy, which also speeds up the reaction.

text: The half-reaction for substance A is a five-electron reduction with a standard cell potential of +1.5 volts, while the half-reaction for substance B is a two-electron reduction with a standard cell potential of +1.6 volts. In volts, what would be the electrode potential of a galvanic cell containing these two substances?
explainAnswer: Identify the half-reaction for substance A and its standard cell potential of +1.5 volts.
Identify the half-reaction for substance B and its standard cell potential of +1.6 volts.
Determine the total number of electrons transferred in the overall reaction by finding a common multiple of the electrons involved in both half-reactions.
Calculate the overall cell potential by subtracting the standard potential of the anode (substance A) from the cathode (substance B).
Simplify the result to find the electrode potential of the galvanic cell.

text: Born-Haber cycles are an application of what law that states that a series of reactions can be combined to determine the enthalpy change of a reaction in question?
explainAnswer: Identify the concept of enthalpy changes in chemical reactions.
Recall that Hess's Law states that the total enthalpy change for a reaction is the sum of the enthalpy changes for individual steps.
Understand that Born-Haber cycles utilize this principle to calculate lattice energy.
Recognize that the law allows for the combination of multiple reaction pathways to find the overall enthalpy change.

text: What IUPAC [EYE-you-pack] stem indicates that a molecule has four carbons?
explainAnswer: Identify the IUPAC naming system for organic compounds.
Recall that the prefix for a four-carbon alkane is 'but'.
Understand that 'but' is used in names like butane, butene, etc.
Conclude that the correct IUPAC stem for a molecule with four carbons is 'but'.

text: In which of the following compounds does hydrogen have an oxidation state that is NOT +1?
explainAnswer: Identify the common oxidation state of hydrogen, which is usually +1.
Examine each compound to determine the oxidation state of hydrogen.
In NH3, CH3COOH, and HF, hydrogen has an oxidation state of +1.
In NaH, sodium (Na) has an oxidation state of +1, making hydrogen have an oxidation state of -1.
Conclude that NaH is the compound where hydrogen does not have an oxidation state of +1.

text: Which of the following is closest to the percent by mass of chloroform that is carbon?
explainAnswer: Determine the molecular formula of chloroform, which is CHCl3.
Calculate the molar mass of chloroform by adding the atomic masses: C (12.01 g/mol) + H (1.01 g/mol) + 3 × Cl (35.45 g/mol).
Find the mass of carbon in chloroform, which is the mass of one carbon atom (12.01 g/mol).
Calculate the percent by mass of carbon by dividing the mass of carbon by the total molar mass of chloroform and multiplying by 100.
Compare the calculated percent by mass to the given choices to find the closest value.

text: Kevin performs a titration using sodium hydroxide as the titrant. He finds that the pH at the equivalence point is above 7. What does this imply about the analyte?
explainAnswer: Understand that the equivalence point in a titration indicates that the amount of titrant added is stoichiometrically equivalent to the amount of analyte present.
Recognize that a strong acid titrated with a strong base will have a neutral pH (7) at the equivalence point.
Note that a weak acid titrated with a strong base will result in a pH greater than 7 at the equivalence point due to the formation of a conjugate base.
Conclude that since the pH at the equivalence point is above 7, the analyte must be a weak acid.

text: Which of the following is NOT a strong acid?
explainAnswer: Identify the common strong acids, which typically include hydrochloric acid, hydrobromic acid, and hydroiodic acid.
Recall that strong acids completely dissociate in water.
Recognize that hydrofluoric acid is known to be a weak acid because it does not fully dissociate in solution.
Eliminate the other options as they are all strong acids.

text: A protein chemist isolates a new enzyme. Which of the following techniques, when performed alone, would be most useful for determining its size?
explainAnswer: Identify the goal of the question, which is to determine the size of the enzyme.
Evaluate each technique provided in the choices for its ability to measure molecular size.
Recognize that MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry is specifically designed to measure the mass-to-charge ratio of ions, providing accurate molecular weight.
Eliminate other techniques that do not primarily focus on determining molecular size, such as NMR spectroscopy and elemental analysis.
Conclude that MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry is the most suitable technique for determining the size of the enzyme.

text: Which of the following best explains why calcium sulfate becomes less soluble in water as temperature rises?
choices: Combination reactions become faster at higher temperatures than decomposition reactions
Different hydrates form at higher temperatures, which are less soluble in water
Calcium sulfate decomposes at high temperatures into an insoluble compound
explainAnswer: Identify that the question is asking about the solubility of calcium sulfate in relation to temperature changes.
Recall the concept of exothermic and endothermic reactions, noting that exothermic reactions release heat.
Understand that if the dissolution of calcium sulfate is exothermic, increasing temperature will shift the equilibrium to favor the solid form, thus decreasing solubility.
Eliminate the other choices by considering their relevance to the solubility of calcium sulfate with respect to temperature.

text: Which of the following changes would shift the equilibrium to the left for the exothermic reaction of solid calcium oxide with carbon dioxide gas to yield solid calcium carbonate?
choices: Decreasing the volume of the container
Increasing the pressure in the container by adding an inert gas
Doubling both the forward and reverse rate constants
explainAnswer: Identify that the reaction is exothermic, meaning heat is released.
Recall that increasing temperature shifts the equilibrium position of exothermic reactions to the left.
Eliminate other options by considering their effects on equilibrium: decreasing volume and increasing pressure favor the side with fewer moles of gas.
Recognize that adding an inert gas does not change the equilibrium position as it does not affect the concentration of reactants or products.
Conclude that increasing the temperature is the only change that shifts the equilibrium to the left.

text: If molten sodium is burned in a pure oxygen atmosphere, a salt is formed. Which of the following is the likely identity of this salt?
explainAnswer: Identify the reactants involved in the reaction, which are molten sodium (Na) and pure oxygen (O2).
Consider the possible oxidation states of sodium when it reacts with oxygen.
Determine the most stable compound formed from sodium and oxygen based on their typical bonding behavior.
Evaluate the provided options to see which one corresponds to the expected product of sodium reacting with oxygen.
Select the correct compound, which is sodium peroxide (Na2O2), as the most likely identity of the salt formed.

text: When performing distillation, which of the following substances would be expected to be collected last based on boiling point?
explainAnswer: Identify the boiling points of each substance: Pentane (36°C), Pentanol (118°C), Dipropyl ether (90°C), and Pentanoic acid (186°C).
Compare the boiling points to determine which substance has the highest boiling point.
Recognize that the substance with the highest boiling point will be collected last during distillation.
Conclude that Pentanoic acid, with the highest boiling point of 186°C, is the correct answer.

text: What is the hybridization of the central oxygen atom in water?
explainAnswer: Identify the central atom in the molecule, which is oxygen in water (H2O).
Count the number of electron pairs around the central atom, including both bonding pairs and lone pairs.
In water, oxygen has two bonding pairs (from the two hydrogen atoms) and two lone pairs, making a total of four electron pairs.
Determine the hybridization based on the number of electron pairs; four electron pairs correspond to sp^3 hybridization.

text: Which of the following elements has an electron configuration that follows the simple order of orbital filling?
explainAnswer: Identify the electron configurations of each element based on their atomic numbers.
Determine the order of orbital filling according to the Aufbau principle.
Compare the electron configurations of the elements to see which one follows the expected order of filling.
Select the element that adheres to the simple order of orbital filling, which is Technetium.

text: Identify all of the following three elements that, when inserted into a silicon crystal lattice, would result in a p-type, doped semiconductor: 1) Carbon; 2) Boron; 3) Nitrogen.
explainAnswer: Understand that p-type semiconductors are created by introducing elements that have fewer valence electrons than silicon, which has four valence electrons.
Identify the valence electrons of each element: Carbon has four, Boron has three, and Nitrogen has five.
Determine that only Boron, with three valence electrons, can create 'holes' in the silicon lattice, allowing for p-type conductivity.
Conclude that Boron is the only element from the list that results in a p-type doped semiconductor.

text: What principle states that two electrons cannot have the same quantum numbers?
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the question, which is about quantum mechanics and electron configuration.
Recall the fundamental principles that govern the behavior of electrons in atoms.
Recognize that the principle stating that no two electrons can occupy the same quantum state is a key concept in quantum mechanics.
Conclude that this principle is known as the Pauli Exclusion Principle.

text: What theory of chemical kinetics states that molecules must come into contact with each other to react?
explainAnswer: Identify the key concept related to chemical reactions and their rates.
Recall that for a reaction to occur, reactant molecules must collide.
Understand that the frequency and energy of these collisions affect the reaction rate.
Conclude that the theory explaining this requirement is known as Collision Theory.

text: What is the oxidation state of the sulfur atom in the sulfate ion?
explainAnswer: Identify the chemical formula of the sulfate ion, which is SO4^2-.
Assign the oxidation state of oxygen, which is typically -2.
Calculate the total oxidation state contributed by the four oxygen atoms: 4 * (-2) = -8.
Set up the equation for the overall charge of the sulfate ion: x + (-8) = -2, where x is the oxidation state of sulfur.
Solve for x: x = -2 + 8, resulting in x = +6.

text: Identify all of the following three molecules that typically undergo an Sn1 reaction in the presence of a nucleophile: 1) Methyl-bromide; 2) 2-bromo-propane; 3) Tert-butyl-amine [turt-BYOO-til-ah-MEEN].
explainAnswer: Identify the structure of each molecule to determine the type of carbon they contain (primary, secondary, or tertiary).
Recall that Sn1 reactions typically occur with tertiary and some secondary carbocations due to their stability.

Evaluate the stability of the carbocation formed by each molecule: methyl-bromide forms a primary carbocation, 2-bromo-propane forms a secondary carbocation, and tert-butyl-amine does not undergo Sn1 as it is not a halide.
Conclude that only 2-bromo-propane can undergo an Sn1 reaction due to the formation of a stable secondary carbocation.

text: What is the oxidation state of chromium in the coordination compound of charge +3 that is formed from the reaction of five ammonia ligands and one chloride ligand with the central chromium ion?
explainAnswer: Identify the total charge of the coordination compound, which is +3.
Recognize that ammonia (NH3) is a neutral ligand and contributes 0 to the oxidation state.
Note that chloride (Cl-) has a charge of -1.
Set up the equation for the oxidation state of chromium (Cr) as x + 5(0) + (-1) = +3.
Solve for x: x - 1 = 3, thus x = +4.

text: A carboxylic [CAR-box-IHL-ik] acid is stirred in a large excess of ethanol in the presence of a sulfuric acid catalyst. What functional group will this reaction form?
explainAnswer: Identify the reactants: a carboxylic acid and ethanol.
Recognize that sulfuric acid acts as a catalyst in the reaction.
Recall that the reaction between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol typically forms an ester.
Eliminate other options based on the functional groups involved in the reaction.

text: A physical chemist has determined the vapor pressure of a liquid at multiple temperatures and wants to determine the standard entropy of vaporization. Which of the following sets of axes will enable the chemist to graph the data as a line and determine the entropy from the y- intercept?
choices: Pressure on y, temperature on x
One over pressure on y, temperature on x
Natural log of pressure on y, temperature on x
Natural log of pressure on y, one over temperature on x
explainAnswer: Understand that the relationship between vapor pressure and temperature can be described by the Clausius-Clapeyron equation.
Identify that the equation can be rearranged to a linear form: ln(P) = -ΔHvap/R(1/T) + C.
Recognize that plotting ln(P) on the y-axis and 1/T on the x-axis will yield a straight line.
Determine that the slope of this line is related to the enthalpy of vaporization, and the y-intercept will help in calculating the standard entropy of vaporization.
Select the correct axes based on this linear relationship, which are natural log of pressure on the y-axis and one over temperature on the x-axis.

text: Which of the following is a diprotic acid:
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of a diprotic acid, which is an acid that can donate two protons (H+ ions).
Examine each option to determine how many protons each acid can donate.
H<sub>2</sub>C<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> (oxalic acid) can donate two protons, making it diprotic.
H<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub> (phosphoric acid) is also diprotic, but the question asks for the correct answer among the choices.
Confirm that HCl and HNO<sub>2</sub> are monoprotic acids, as they can only donate one proton.

text: Which of the following alkali metals has the most negative standard reduction potential?
explainAnswer: Understand that standard reduction potential indicates how easily a species can be reduced.
Recognize that alkali metals have a trend in reduction potentials that becomes more negative as you move down the group.
Identify the alkali metals in the question: Sodium, Potassium, Rubidium, and Cesium.
Recall that Cesium is the heaviest alkali metal listed, and therefore has the most negative standard reduction potential.
Conclude that Cesium is the correct answer based on its position in the periodic table.

text: Hans Bethe is famous for the development of what theory of coordination in which metal-ligand [LIH-gund] interactions are assumed to be completely ionic?
explainAnswer: Identify the key terms in the question, such as 'Hans Bethe' and 'metal-ligand interactions'.
Recall the theories related to coordination chemistry that involve metal-ligand interactions.
Determine which theory assumes completely ionic interactions between metals and ligands.
Conclude that the theory being referred to is Crystal Field Theory.

text: Which of the following polyprotic [polly-PRO-tic] acids has only two pKa values?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of polyprotic acids, which can donate more than one proton.
Review the structure of each acid listed to determine the number of acidic protons.
Count the pKa values for each acid based on the number of protons they can donate.
Determine which acid has exactly two pKa values, confirming that it is Ascorbic acid.

text: Which of the following atoms has at least one completely filled p- subshell?
explainAnswer: Identify the electron configuration of each atom: Sulfur (S) is 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁴, Oxygen (O) is 1s² 2s² 2p⁴, Boron (B) is 1s² 2s² 2p¹, and Helium (He) is 1s².
Determine the p-subshell filling: A completely filled p-subshell contains 6 electrons in the p orbital.
Check the p-subshell of each atom: Sulfur has 4 electrons in its 3p subshell, which is not completely filled, but it has a filled 2p subshell (6 electrons).
Since the question asks for at least one completely filled p-subshell, Sulfur qualifies because its 2p subshell is filled.

text: Order the following three gases from slowest to fastest in terms of their rate of effusion at 25 degrees Celcius: 1) Helium; 2) Argon; 3) Neon.
explainAnswer: Identify the molar masses of the gases: Helium (4 g/mol), Argon (40 g/mol), and Neon (20 g/mol).
Apply Graham's law of effusion, which states that the rate of effusion is inversely proportional to the square root of the molar mass.
Calculate the rate of effusion for each gas: Helium will have the highest rate due to its lowest molar mass, followed by Neon, and then Argon.
Order the gases from slowest to fastest based on their calculated rates of effusion: Argon, Neon, Helium.

text: What property of an element is defined as the amount of energy released when one mole of electrons is added to one mole of the neutral atomic element in the gaseous state?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of electron affinity as it relates to energy changes in atomic interactions.
Understand that electron affinity specifically refers to the energy change when an electron is added to a neutral atom.
Recognize that this process is measured in moles, specifically one mole of electrons and one mole of the atomic element.
Conclude that the correct term for this property is electron affinity.

text: A student obtained a low value when he attempted to measure the number of waters of hydration in a sample of calcium sulfate. Which of the following mistakes could lead to the erroneous result?
choices: The sample was not heated enough
The sample was heated too much
A balance that gave uniformly high readings was used
A balance that gave uniformly low readings was used
explainAnswer: Identify the process of measuring waters of hydration, which involves heating the sample to remove water.
Consider the effects of insufficient heating on the measurement, as it would leave some water in the sample.
Evaluate the other options and determine that excessive heating, or using a balance with consistent high or low readings, would not specifically result in a low measurement of waters of hydration.
Conclude that not heating the sample enough would lead to an inaccurate, low value for the waters of hydration.

text: Identify all of the following three reactions that would result in a precipitate. 1) Addition of iron(III) nitrate to sodium sulfate; 2) Addition of aluminum nitrate and zinc sulfate; 3) Addition of iron(III) nitrate to sodium hydroxide.
explainAnswer: Identify the ions present in each reaction.
Determine the solubility rules for the resulting compounds.
Check if any of the combinations of ions form an insoluble compound, which would indicate a precipitate.
Conclude which reactions produce a precipitate based on the solubility results.

text: Selenous acid is a weak diprotic acid with formula H<sub>2</sub>SeO<sub>3</sub>. Its first pKa value is 2.5 and its second is 7.3. To one decimal place, what is the pH of a 1 molar solution of sodium hydroselenite, the amphiprotic salt of selenous acid?
explainAnswer: Identify that sodium hydroselenite (NaHSeO3) acts as a weak base in solution.
Use the pKa values of selenous acid to determine the relevant equilibrium, focusing on the second dissociation.
Calculate the pKb of the conjugate base (HSeO3-) using the relation pKw = pKa + pKb.
Use the formula for pH, where pH = 14 - pKb for a weak base, to find the pH of the solution.
Substitute the values into the equation to find the final pH, rounding to one decimal place.

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true regarding spontaneity of a reaction: 1) A more spontaneous reaction produces a larger proportion of product than a less spontaneous one; 2) A more spontaneous reaction occurs more quickly than a less spontaneous one; 3) A more spontaneous reaction always has a greater magnitude Gibbs free energy change than a less spontaneous one.
explainAnswer: Evaluate the definition of spontaneity in chemical reactions, which relates to the favorability of product formation.
Analyze statement 1, recognizing that a more spontaneous reaction indeed produces a larger proportion of products.
Consider statement 2, noting that spontaneity does not directly correlate with the rate of reaction, as a spontaneous reaction can still be slow.
Examine statement 3, understanding that spontaneity is indicated by the sign of the Gibbs free energy change, not necessarily its magnitude.

text: Identify all of the following three quantities that increase when the electron in a hydrogen atom transitions from 1s to 2s: 1) Energy of the electron; 2) Value of azimuthal quantum number; 3) Value of principal quantum number.
explainAnswer: Identify the principal quantum number (n) for each state: 1s has n=1 and 2s has n=2.
Determine the energy levels of the electron in each state: energy increases with increasing n.
Check the azimuthal quantum number (l) for each state: 1s has l=0 and 2s also has l=0, which does not increase.
Conclude that the energy of the electron increases and the principal quantum number increases, while the azimuthal quantum number does not increase.

text: Which of the following atoms has an atomic radius closest to the atomic radius of sodium?
explainAnswer: Identify the atomic radius trend in the periodic table, which generally increases down a group and decreases across a period.
Locate sodium (Na) in the periodic table and note its position in group 1 (alkali metals).
Compare the atomic radii of the given choices, focusing on elements in the same group or nearby groups.
Determine that calcium (Ca), being in group 2 and below sodium, has an atomic radius that is closer to sodium than the other options.

text: Identify all of the following three organic compounds that can be used as strong bases in a chemical reaction: 1) Pyridinium chloro-chromate; 2) Oxolane; 3) DMSO.
explainAnswer: Understand that strong bases are typically substances that can readily donate hydroxide ions (OH-) or accept protons (H+).
Evaluate each compound: Pyridinium chloro-chromate is a strong oxidizing agent, not a base.
Oxolane (tetrahydrofuran) is a solvent and does not have strong basic properties.
DMSO (dimethyl sulfoxide) is a polar aprotic solvent and does not act as a strong base.
Conclude that none of the listed compounds qualify as strong bases.

text: Rank the following three ions in terms of increasing radius: 1) Na+ [N A plus] ; 2) Be2+ [B E plus two] ; 3) Li+ [L I plus] .
explainAnswer: Identify that all three ions are cations with a positive charge, which means they have lost electrons.
Recognize that as the positive charge increases (from Li+ to Be2+), the effective nuclear charge on the remaining electrons also increases, pulling them closer to the nucleus.

Compare the ionic sizes: Li+ has the largest radius because it has the least positive charge, followed by Na+ with a single positive charge, and Be2+ with the highest positive charge, making it the smallest.

text: Which of the following acids is stronger than hydrofluoric acid?
explainAnswer: Identify the strength of hydrofluoric acid (HF) as a weak acid.
Research the strength of the given acids: iodic acid, formic acid, acetic acid, and hypochlorous acid.
Compare the acid dissociation constants (Ka) or pKa values of these acids to determine their relative strengths.
Determine that iodic acid has a higher dissociation constant than hydrofluoric acid, indicating it is a stronger acid.

text: Identify all of the following three species that are Lewis acids: 1) Zn<sup>2+</sup>; 2) Cl<sup>−</sup>; 3) BH<sub>3</sub>.
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of a Lewis acid as a species that can accept an electron pair.
Evaluate Zn<sup>2+</sup>: it has a positive charge and can accept electron pairs, so it is a Lewis acid.
Evaluate Cl<sup>−</sup>: it has a negative charge and typically donates electron pairs, so it is not a Lewis acid.
Evaluate BH<sub>3</sub>: it has an incomplete octet and can accept electron pairs, making it a Lewis acid.
Conclude that the Lewis acids among the given species are Zn<sup>2+</sup> and BH<sub>3</sub>.

text: Which of the following 1.0 molar solutions will have the largest change in boiling point from that of pure water?
explainAnswer: Identify the van 't Hoff factor (i)' for each solute, which indicates the number of particles the solute dissociates into in solution.

Calculate the total number of particles for each solute: Sodium bromide (NaBr) dissociates into 2 particles, Magnesium iodide (MgI2) into 3 particles, Sucrose (C12H22O11) remains as 1 particle, and Potassium phosphate (K3PO4) into 4 particles.
Determine the change in boiling point for each solution using the formula ΔT_b = i * K_b * m, where K_b is the ebullioscopic constant and m is the molality (1.0 molar in this case).
Compare the calculated changes in boiling points to find which solute causes the largest increase.

text: Rank the following three barium salts in terms of increasing water solubility: 1) Barium chlorate; 2) Barium sulfate; 3) Barium hydroxide.
explainAnswer: Recall the general solubility rules for salts in water.
Identify that barium sulfate is known to be insoluble in water.
Recognize that barium hydroxide is moderately soluble in water.
Understand that barium chlorate is highly soluble in water.
Rank the salts from least to most soluble: barium sulfate (2), barium hydroxide (3), barium chlorate (1).

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true regarding enthalpies of reaction: 1) For the formation of water from oxygen and hydrogen, the enthalpy [EN-thul- pee] change depends on the final phase of the water; 2) For the combustion of methane, the forward reaction and the reverse reaction have the same enthalpy; 3) Enthalpy is an intensive property.
explainAnswer: Evaluate each statement regarding enthalpy changes in reactions.
For statement 1, recognize that the enthalpy change for the formation of water can vary based on whether water is in gas, liquid, or solid phase.
For statement 2, understand that the forward and reverse reactions have equal but opposite enthalpy changes, so this statement is false.
For statement 3, recall that enthalpy is an extensive property, not intensive, making this statement false.
Conclude that only statement 1 is true.

text: Which of the following metals will not readily react with cold water to generate hydrogen gas and the corresponding metal hydroxide due to the existence of a nonreactive metal oxide layer coating the metal?
explainAnswer: Identify the metals listed in the choices and their reactivity with water.
Recall that some metals form a protective oxide layer that inhibits further reactions.
Determine which of the listed metals is known to form a nonreactive oxide layer.
Conclude that aluminum is the metal that does not readily react with cold water due to its oxide layer.

text: Which of the following values for oxygen will be larger than the corresponding value for boron?
explainAnswer: Identify the periodic trends for atomic radius, ionization energy, melting point, and metallic character.
Recall that ionization energy generally increases across a period and decreases down a group in the periodic table.
Locate oxygen and boron on the periodic table to compare their positions and corresponding trends.
Determine that oxygen, being further to the right in the same period as boron, has a higher ionization energy than boron.

text: Which of the following best describes the kinetics of radioactive decay?
choices: It is a zeroth order process
It is a first order process
It is a second order process
It is a third order process
explainAnswer: Understand that radioactive decay is a process where the quantity of a radioactive substance decreases over time.
Recall that first order kinetics means the rate of decay is proportional to the amount of substance remaining.
Recognize that the half-life of a substance in first order kinetics is constant and independent of the initial amount.
Eliminate the other order processes (zeroth, second, third) based on their definitions and characteristics.
Conclude that radioactive decay is best described as a first order process.

text: What is the point on a phase diagram that represents the temperature and pressure at which three phases of a substance can coexist?
explainAnswer: Understand that a phase diagram illustrates the states of matter (solid, liquid, gas) of a substance at various temperatures and pressures.
Identify the region on the phase diagram where the boundaries of the three phases meet.
Recognize that the specific point where these boundaries intersect is known as the triple point.
Conclude that the triple point is the temperature and pressure at which all three phases can coexist.

text: Which of the following acids is triprotic [try-PRO-tic]?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of a triprotic acid, which is an acid that can donate three protons (H+ ions).
Examine each of the given acids to determine how many protons they can donate.
Sulfuric acid is diprotic, hydrocyanic acid is monoprotic, and pyruvic acid is also monoprotic.
Arsenic acid is known to be triprotic as it can donate three protons.
Conclude that arsenic acid is the correct answer.

text: Molten cryolite is used in what industrial process?
explainAnswer: Identify the properties and uses of cryolite in industrial applications.
Research the processes that utilize cryolite, focusing on aluminum production.
Determine the specific process associated with the use of molten cryolite.
Confirm that the Hall-Héroult process is the primary method for aluminum extraction using cryolite.

text: Which of the following alkaline metal hydroxides has the highest solubility in water?
explainAnswer: Recall that alkaline earth metal hydroxides generally increase in solubility down the group from magnesium to barium.
Compare the solubility of each hydroxide in water based on known solubility trends.
Identify that barium hydroxide is known to be more soluble than magnesium, calcium, and strontium hydroxides.
Conclude that barium hydroxide has the highest solubility among the given options.

text: Which of the following is the energy in joules of a photon with a frequency of 1.00 x 10<sup>6</sup> gigahertz?
explainAnswer: Convert the frequency from gigahertz to hertz by multiplying by 10^9.
Use the formula E = h * f, where E is energy, h is Planck's constant (6.63 x 10^-34 J·s), and f is the frequency in hertz.
Calculate the energy by substituting the values into the formula.
Simplify the result to find the energy in joules.

text: Identify all of the following three organic reactions in which carbon atoms are reduced: 1) Transformation of alkanes into alcohols; 2) Transformation of ketones into secondary alcohols; 3) Transformation of carboxylic acids into aldehydes.
explainAnswer: Understand that reduction in organic chemistry involves the gain of electrons or hydrogen atoms, or the loss of oxygen atoms.
Analyze each transformation: 1) Alkanes to alcohols involves oxidation, not reduction, as it typically requires the addition of oxygen.
For 2) Ketones to secondary alcohols, recognize that this reaction involves the addition of hydrogen, indicating a reduction process.
For 3) Carboxylic acids to aldehydes, note that this reaction involves the removal of an oxygen atom, which is also indicative of reduction.
Conclude that only transformations 2 and 3 involve the reduction of carbon atoms.

text: What named pericyclic reaction is classically the reaction of a di-ene [DYE-een] with a dienophile [dye-EENOH-file] in a single, concerted step?
explainAnswer: Identify the components of the reaction: a diene and a dienophile.
Recognize that the reaction occurs in a single, concerted step.
Recall that this specific type of reaction is a named pericyclic reaction.
Conclude that the named reaction is the Diels-Alder reaction.

text: What neutral nitrogen oxide contains nitrogen atoms with an average oxidation number of +3?
explainAnswer: Identify the neutral nitrogen oxides, which include N2O, NO, NO2, and N2O3.
Determine the oxidation states of nitrogen in each oxide.
Calculate the average oxidation number of nitrogen for each compound.
Identify which compound has an average oxidation number of +3, which is N2O3.

text: Identify all of the following three elements that are considered nonmetals: 1) Radon; 2) Europium; 3) Americium.
explainAnswer: Recall the periodic table classification of elements into metals, nonmetals, and metalloids.
Identify the atomic numbers and positions of Radon, Europium, and Americium on the periodic table.
Determine that Radon is located in Group 18, which is known for nonmetals, while Europium and Americium are in the lanthanide and actinide series, respectively, which are metals.
Conclude that only Radon is a nonmetal among the three elements listed.

text: An SN1 reaction is performed by reacting sodium bromide with (S)-2-chlorobutane, and generates a 1 molar mixture of 70% (S)-2-bromobutane and 30% (R)-2-bromobutane. If the optical rotation of the solution was 9.2°, what is the optical rotation of pure (S)-2-bromobutane, to the nearest degree?
explainAnswer: Determine the contribution of each enantiomer to the optical rotation based on their percentages.
Calculate the specific rotation for the mixture using the formula: observed rotation = (percentage of (S) * specific rotation of (S)) + (percentage of (R) * specific rotation of (R)).
Since (R)-2-bromobutane is the enantiomer of (S)-2-bromobutane, its specific rotation will be the negative of (S)-2-bromobutane's specific rotation.
Set up the equation with the known values: 9.2° = (0.7 * specific rotation of (S)) + (0.3 * (-specific rotation of (S))).
Solve for the specific rotation of (S)-2-bromobutane to find the answer.

text: Nitrogen monoxide is an example of which of the following?
explainAnswer: Identify the molecular structure of nitrogen monoxide (NO) and its electron configuration.
Determine if NO has an unpaired electron, which is characteristic of free radicals.
Evaluate the definitions of the other options to confirm they do not apply to NO.
Conclude that since NO has an unpaired electron, it is classified as a free radical.

text: Consider the reaction of hydrogen and iodine gases to form hydrogen iodide gas at 800 kelvins. If 0.7 moles each of hydrogen and iodine gases are introduced into a one-liter container, and there are 0.6 moles of hydrogen iodide at equilibrium, what is the K<sub>C</sub> for this reaction?
explainAnswer: Determine the initial moles of hydrogen and iodine, which are both 0.7 moles.
Write the balanced equation for the reaction: H2(g) + I2(g) ⇌ 2 HI(g).
Calculate the change in moles of H2 and I2 at equilibrium, which is 0.6 moles of HI produced, leading to a decrease of 0.3 moles for each of H2 and I2.
Determine the equilibrium moles of H2 and I2: 0.7 - 0.3 = 0.4 moles for each.
Use the equilibrium concentrations to calculate K_C using the formula K_C = [HI]^2 / ([H2][I2]) = (0.6^2) / (0.4 * 0.4) = 2.25.

text: What class of organic molecules has the formula R-COOH and can react with alcohols to produce esters?
explainAnswer: Identify the functional group represented by the formula R-COOH, which indicates the presence of a carboxyl group.
Recognize that the R represents a hydrocarbon chain or hydrogen atom, making it a general representation of carboxylic acids.
Recall that carboxylic acids can react with alcohols in a condensation reaction to form esters.
Conclude that the class of organic molecules described by the formula R-COOH is indeed carboxylic acids.

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are TRUE of ideal concentration cells: 1) They obey the Nernst equation; 2) At equilibrium, they have a positive redox [REE-dox] potential; 3) They have a positive standard redox potential.
explainAnswer: Understand that ideal concentration cells operate based on the Nernst equation, which relates the cell potential to the concentrations of the reactants and products.
Evaluate each statement individually: statement 1 is true because ideal concentration cells do obey the Nernst equation.
Consider statement 2, which is false because at equilibrium, the cell potential is zero, not positive.
Assess statement 3, which is also false because ideal concentration cells can have a standard redox potential that is zero or negative depending on the concentrations used.

text: When sodium chloride is dissolved in water, each ion is surrounded by a cluster of water molecules called what?
explainAnswer: Recall the process of ionic compounds dissolving in water.
Identify the interaction between water molecules and the ions.
Recognize that the surrounding water molecules form a specific structure around each ion.
Define this structure as the solvation shell or hydration.

text: Identify all of the following three quantites in reaction kinetics that are dimensionless: 1) Rate constant; 2) Steric [steh-rik] factor; 3) Collision frequency.
explainAnswer: Understand that a dimensionless quantity has no units associated with it.

Identify the definitions of each quantity: rate constant has units depending on the order of the reaction, steric factor is a ratio and thus dimensionless, and collision frequency has units of frequency.
Conclude that the only dimensionless quantity among the three is the steric factor.

text: Nitric oxide contains 10 electrons in bonding orbitals and 5 electrons in antibonding orbitals. What is its bond order?
explainAnswer: Identify the number of electrons in bonding orbitals, which is 10.
Identify the number of electrons in antibonding orbitals, which is 5.
Use the bond order formula: Bond Order = (Number of bonding electrons - Number of antibonding electrons) / 2.
Substitute the values into the formula: Bond Order = (10 - 5) / 2.
Calculate the bond order, which results in 2.5.

text: In degrees, which of the following is closest to the bond angle between hydrogen atoms in ammonia?
explainAnswer: Recall that ammonia (NH3) has a trigonal pyramidal molecular geometry.
Understand that the ideal bond angle for a tetrahedral arrangement is 109.5 degrees.
Recognize that the presence of a lone pair of electrons in ammonia slightly reduces the bond angle.
Determine that the bond angle in ammonia is approximately 107-109 degrees, making 108 the closest option.

text: Which of the electron's quantum numbers corresponds to the size and energy of the orbital?
explainAnswer: Identify the four quantum numbers: principal, azimuthal, magnetic, and spin.
Understand that the principal quantum number (n) indicates the main energy level of an electron.
Recognize that a higher principal quantum number corresponds to a larger orbital size and higher energy.
Conclude that the principal quantum number is the one that corresponds to the size and energy of the orbital.

text: Which of the following is the general formula for a noncyclic alkene with n number of carbon atoms:
explainAnswer: Recall that alkenes are hydrocarbons containing at least one carbon-carbon double bond.
Determine the general formula for alkenes, which is derived from the fact that each double bond reduces the number of hydrogen atoms by two compared to alkanes.
Recognize that the general formula for alkanes is C_nH_(2n+2), and removing one double bond leads to C_nH_(2n).
Select the option that matches the derived formula for noncyclic alkenes, which is C_nH_(2n).

text: Which of the following neutral ground state atoms has the lowest ionization energy?
explainAnswer: Identify the trend of ionization energy in the periodic table, which generally increases across a period and decreases down a group.
Locate the elements in the same period: Carbon (C), Boron (B), Nitrogen (N), and Oxygen (O) are all in period 2.
Compare the positions of these elements; Boron is to the left of Carbon, Nitrogen, and Oxygen.
Since ionization energy decreases from left to right in a period, Boron has the lowest ionization energy among the given choices.

text: For calcium, which of the following energy sublevels is closest in energy to the 4s sublevel?
explainAnswer: Identify the principal quantum numbers of the sublevels: 3s, 3d, 4s, 4p, and 4d.
Recognize that sublevels with the same principal quantum number (n) are generally closer in energy.
Compare the energy levels of the sublevels: 3d is in the n=3 level and is typically higher in energy than 3s but lower than 4s.
Determine that among the given options, 3d is the closest in energy to the 4s sublevel.

text: Lithium aluminum hydride would likely be used by a synthetic chemist for what type of reaction?
explainAnswer: Identify the functional groups involved in the reactions listed in the choices.
Recall that lithium aluminum hydride (LiAlH4) is a strong reducing agent.
Determine which reaction type typically involves the addition of hydrogen or the removal of oxygen.
Recognize that reduction reactions are characterized by the gain of electrons or hydrogen, which aligns with the properties of LiAlH4.
Conclude that the correct answer is Reduction based on the role of LiAlH4.

text: What type of reaction converts a single stereoisomer into an equal mixture of both stereoisomers?
explainAnswer: Identify the type of reaction that involves the conversion of one stereoisomer into another.
Understand that racemization specifically refers to the process of converting one enantiomer into a 1:1 mixture of both enantiomers.
Recognize that this reaction typically involves breaking and reforming bonds to allow for the interconversion of stereoisomers.
Conclude that the correct term for this reaction is racemization.

text: A supersaturated solution of sodium nitrate was prepared at 80 degrees Celsius but cooled to room temperature. Which of the following statements describes the addition of a seed crystal?
choices: Delta H is negative and Delta S is negative
Delta H is positive and Delta S is negative
Delta H is negative and Delta S is positive
Delta H is positive and Delta S is positive
explainAnswer: Identify that adding a seed crystal to a supersaturated solution initiates crystallization.
Recognize that the process of crystallization releases heat, indicating that Delta H is negative.
Understand that the formation of a solid from a solution decreases the disorder of the system, leading to a negative Delta S.
Combine these observations to conclude that the correct choice is Delta H is negative and Delta S is negative.

text: What is the systematic name of tert-butyl [turt-BYOO-til] chloride?
explainAnswer: Identify the structure of tert-butyl chloride, which consists of a tert-butyl group (a central carbon bonded to three methyl groups) and a chlorine atom.
Determine the position of the chlorine atom on the carbon chain; in this case, it is attached to the second carbon of the propane chain.
Name the carbon chain by counting the total number of carbons, which gives 'propane' for three carbons.
Add the substituent name 'chloro' to indicate the presence of the chlorine atom, placing it before the name of the main chain.
Combine the information to form the systematic name: 2-chloro-2-methylpropane.

text: Consider a 12-gram sample of carbon-12. What is the name for the constant one obtains by dividing the mass of this sample by the atomic mass of carbon-12?
explainAnswer: Identify the mass of the carbon-12 sample, which is 12 grams.
Determine the atomic mass of carbon-12, which is defined as 12 atomic mass units (amu).
Divide the mass of the sample (12 grams) by the atomic mass (12 amu) to find the number of moles.
Recognize that this value represents Avogadro's number, which is the number of atoms in one mole of a substance.

text: Which of the following is NOT true of glucose:
choices: when glucose joins with galactose, fructose is formed
cellulose is a polymer of glucose molecules
explainAnswer: Identify the properties and reactions of glucose mentioned in the choices.
Recall that glucose and galactose combine to form lactose, not fructose.
Verify the other statements about glucose to confirm their accuracy.
Conclude that the statement about glucose forming fructose with galactose is incorrect.

text: To measure the number of moles of barium in a solution containing both magnesium<sup>2+</sup> and barium<sup>2+</sup> ions, a student added sodium sulfate and collected the precipitate. Then, he weighed the precipitate, and used stoichiometric conversions to estimate the number of moles of barium, and discovered that his method over-reported the actual value stated by his teacher. Which of the following plausibly explains the discrepancy?
choices: The student precipitated both magnesium and barium when adding sodium sulfate
The student used a molar mass for barium that was 10% too high
The student used a molar mass for sulfur that was 10% too high
The student didn’t properly dry his precipitate before weighing
explainAnswer: Identify the components of the precipitate formed when sodium sulfate is added to the solution.
Consider the possible sources of error in measuring the mass of the precipitate.
Evaluate how not properly drying the precipitate could lead to an overestimation of its mass.
Determine how an overestimated mass would affect the calculated number of moles of barium.
Conclude that the student's method over-reported the moles of barium due to the excess water weight in the precipitate.

text: Consider the gas-phase decomposition of PCl<sub>5</sub> into PCl<sub>3</sub> and Cl<sub>2</sub>. If the reaction begins with 5 atmospheres of PCl<sub>5</sub>, and if the partial pressure of chlorine is x atm at equilibrium, which of the following expressions for K<sub>p</sub> is correct?
choices: The fraction with numerator x and denominator 5 minus x
The fraction with numerator x and denominator open parenthesis 5 minus x close parenthesis squared
The fraction with numerator x squared and denominator 5 minus x
The fraction with numerator x squared and denominator open parenthesis 5 minus x close parenthesis squared
explainAnswer: Identify the balanced chemical equation for the decomposition of PCl5 into PCl3 and Cl2.
Set up an ICE table (Initial, Change, Equilibrium) to track the changes in partial pressures of the reactants and products.
Express the equilibrium partial pressures in terms of x, where x is the partial pressure of Cl2 at equilibrium.
Write the expression for Kp based on the equilibrium concentrations: Kp = (PCl3)(PCl2) / (PCl5).
Substitute the expressions for the partial pressures into the Kp formula to find the correct expression.

text: Consider ice at 0 degrees Celsius that is heated until it becomes water at 80 degrees Celsius. Which of the following statements is TRUE concerning its volume?
choices: It decreases until 4 degrees Celsius, then increases
It increases until 4 degrees Celsius, then remains constant
explainAnswer: Understand that ice has a lower density than water, which means its volume will change as it transitions from solid to liquid.
Recognize that as ice is heated from 0 degrees Celsius to 4 degrees Celsius, it will contract and its volume will decrease.
Identify that at 4 degrees Celsius, water reaches its maximum density, and any further heating will cause the volume to increase as it turns into water at higher temperatures.
Conclude that the volume decreases until 4 degrees Celsius and then increases as the temperature rises above 4 degrees Celsius.

text: Which of the following quantum numbers describes the shape of the orbital?
explainAnswer: Identify the different types of quantum numbers: principal, azimuthal, magnetic, and spin.
Understand that the principal quantum number describes the energy level of an electron.
Recognize that the azimuthal quantum number defines the shape of the orbital (s, p, d, f).
Note that the magnetic quantum number relates to the orientation of the orbital, and the spin quantum number describes the spin of the electron.
Conclude that the azimuthal quantum number is the one that specifically describes the shape of the orbital.

text: Which of the following compounds or ions is the best oxidizing agent?
explainAnswer: Identify the oxidation states of the elements in each compound or ion.
Determine which species has the highest tendency to gain electrons or undergo reduction.
Recall that a good oxidizing agent is one that is easily reduced.
Compare the standard reduction potentials of the given options if available.
Conclude that MnO<sub>2</sub> is the best oxidizing agent based on its ability to accept electrons.

text: N<sub>2</sub>O is in equilibrium with N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> in a transparent cylinder fitted with a piston. Identify all of the following three changes that would increase the number of N<sub>2</sub>O molecules in the cylinder: 1) Depressing the piston; 2) Increasing the temperature; 3) Adding nitrogen gas.
explainAnswer: Understand that the equilibrium between N2O and N2O4 can be affected by changes in temperature and concentration.
Recognize that increasing the temperature favors the endothermic reaction, which in this case is the decomposition of N2O4 into N2O.
Evaluate the effect of depressing the piston and adding nitrogen gas, noting that these actions do not directly increase N2O molecules in the equilibrium context.

text: Rank the following three diatomic molecules in order of increasing bond dissociation energy: 1) Nitrogen; 2) Oxygen; 3) Fluorine.
explainAnswer: Identify the bond order of each diatomic molecule: Nitrogen (N2) has a triple bond, Oxygen (O2) has a double bond, and Fluorine (F2) has a single bond.
Recall that higher bond order generally corresponds to higher bond dissociation energy.
Rank the molecules based on their bond orders: F2 has the lowest bond order, O2 has a higher bond order, and N2 has the highest bond order.
Conclude that the order of increasing bond dissociation energy is Fluorine (F2), Oxygen (O2), and Nitrogen (N2).

text: Concentrated hydrochloric acid is sold as a 12-molar solution in water. How many milliliters of concentrated hydrochloric acid must be used to prepare 1.5 liters of a 100-millimolar solution of hydrochloric acid?
explainAnswer: Convert the final volume of the desired solution from liters to milliliters by multiplying 1.5 liters by 1000, resulting in 1500 milliliters.
Calculate the amount of hydrochloric acid needed in millimoles by multiplying the final concentration (100 millimolar) by the final volume (1500 milliliters), giving 150 millimoles.
Since the concentrated solution is 12 molar, convert this to millimoles per milliliter by noting that 12 molar is equivalent to 12 millimoles per milliliter.
Divide the total millimoles needed (150 millimoles) by the concentration of the stock solution (12 millimoles per milliliter) to find the volume needed in milliliters, which is 12.5 milliliters.

text: Kate is performing an experiment where she has a chamber containing an inert gas. The chamber is at a fixed temperature and she varies the pressure of the chamber. She generates a curve by plotting pressure on the x-axis and PV over RT on the y-axis. At which of the following fixed chamber temperatures, in kelvins, would this curve be the MOST linear?
explainAnswer: Understand that the ideal gas law is PV = nRT, which can be rearranged to plot PV/RT against pressure.
Recognize that as temperature increases, the behavior of real gases approaches ideal gas behavior.
Identify that a more linear relationship on the graph indicates closer adherence to ideal gas behavior.
Evaluate the given temperatures and determine that 1500 K is the highest temperature, suggesting the most ideal behavior.
Conclude that at 1500 K, the curve will be the most linear due to the gas behaving more ideally.

text: What rule in organic synthesis states that the more electropositive of a reacting species tends to bond to the least-highly-substituted carbon atom in an alkene [al-KEEN] during an addition reaction?
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the question, which is about organic synthesis and addition reactions.
Recall the concept of regioselectivity in reactions involving alkenes.
Understand that Markovnikov's Rule describes the behavior of electrophiles in these reactions.
Recognize that the more electropositive species will bond to the least substituted carbon atom of the alkene.
Conclude that the name of this rule is Markovnikov's Rule.

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true of bonding: 1) Xenon dichloride has a bent molecular geometry; 2) Sulfur dioxide and carbon disulfide have the same molecular geometry; 3) Krypton tetrafluoride has no net dipole moment.
explainAnswer: Evaluate the molecular geometry of xenon dichloride to determine if it is bent or not.
Compare the molecular geometries of sulfur dioxide and carbon disulfide to see if they are the same.
Analyze the molecular structure of krypton tetrafluoride to check if it has a net dipole moment.

text: Which of the following statements concerning hydrogen bonding is NOT true?
choices: Amines [ah-MEENS] can act as hydrogen bond donors and acceptors
Ethers can form hydrogen bonds with each other
The salicylate [sah-LIH-sil -ate] anion [AN-eye-on] is stabilized by intramolecular hydrogen bonding
Hydrogen sulfide cannot engage in hydrogen bonding
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of hydrogen bonding, including donors and acceptors.
Evaluate each statement to determine if it correctly describes the ability of the substances to engage in hydrogen bonding.
Recall that ethers lack hydrogen atoms bonded to highly electronegative atoms, which are necessary for hydrogen bonding.
Conclude that the statement about ethers forming hydrogen bonds with each other is false.

text: Which of the following molecules has T-shaped molecular geometry?
explainAnswer: Identify the central atom in each molecule and count the number of bonding pairs and lone pairs of electrons.
Use the VSEPR theory to determine the molecular geometry based on the arrangement of bonding and lone pairs.
For ClF3, recognize that it has 3 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs, which leads to a T-shaped geometry.
Eliminate the other options by analyzing their bonding and lone pair configurations to confirm they do not have T-shaped geometry.

text: What is the conjugate acid of ammonia?
explainAnswer: Identify the base in question, which is ammonia (NH3).
Recall that the conjugate acid is formed when a base accepts a proton (H+).
Add a proton to ammonia (NH3) to form ammonium (NH4+).
Conclude that the conjugate acid of ammonia is ammonium (NH4+).

text: Di-iodine gas can dissociate into two atoms of iodine gas. At 1200 kelvins, the forward reaction has an equilibrium constant of approximately 10. In kilojoules per mole, which of the following is closest to the standard change in Gibbs free energy of this reaction?
explainAnswer: Identify the relationship between the equilibrium constant (K) and the standard change in Gibbs free energy (ΔG°) using the equation ΔG° = -RT ln(K).
Use the value of R = 8.314 J/(mol·K) and convert it to kJ by dividing by 1000 to get R = 0.008314 kJ/(mol·K).
Substitute the values into the equation: ΔG° = -0.008314 kJ/(mol·K) * 1200 K * ln(10).
Calculate ln(10) which is approximately 2.303, then multiply: ΔG° = -0.008314 * 1200 * 2.303.
Evaluate the expression to find that ΔG° is approximately -20 kJ/mol.

text: Rank the following three elements in order of increasing ionization energy: 1) Krypton; 2) Neon; 3) Fluorine.
explainAnswer: Identify the general trend of ionization energy in the periodic table, which increases across a period and decreases down a group.
Locate Krypton, Neon, and Fluorine on the periodic table: Krypton is in Group 18, Neon is in Group 18, and Fluorine is in Group 17.
Compare the positions of the elements: Krypton is lower than Neon and Fluorine, so it has the lowest ionization energy.
Recognize that Neon, being in the same group as Krypton but higher up, has a higher ionization energy than Krypton but lower than Fluorine.
Conclude that the order of increasing ionization energy is Krypton (1), Fluorine (3), and Neon (2).

text: How many electrons does the beryllium [beh-RILL-ee-um] two plus cation [CAT-eye-on] have in its valence [VAY-lence] shell?
explainAnswer: Identify the atomic number of beryllium, which is 4.
Determine the electron configuration of neutral beryllium, which is 1s² 2s².
Recognize that the beryllium two plus cation (Be²⁺) loses two electrons from its neutral state.
Since the two electrons lost are from the outermost shell (2s), the valence shell now has 0 electrons.
However, the question specifically asks for the number of valence electrons before ionization, which is 2.

text: A student performs combustion analysis on a compound X containing carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen to determine its molecular formula. Given the molar mass is 76, if she combusts 1 mole of X in excess oxygen and observes 2 moles of CO<sub>2</sub> gas and 2 moles of H<sub>2</sub>O gas as products, what is the molecular formula?
explainAnswer: Determine the number of moles of carbon from CO2 produced, which is 2 moles of CO2 indicating 2 moles of carbon.
Determine the number of moles of hydrogen from H2O produced, which is 2 moles of H2O indicating 4 moles of hydrogen.
Assume the remaining mass is due to oxygen, and calculate the total mass of carbon and hydrogen.
Use the molar mass of the compound (76 g/mol) to find the number of moles of oxygen in the compound.
Combine the moles of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen to derive the empirical formula and then adjust to find the molecular formula.

text: The drying step of the freeze-drying process is an example of what type of phase change?
explainAnswer: Identify the process of freeze-drying and its stages.
Recognize that freeze-drying involves removing moisture from a substance.
Understand that sublimation is the transition from solid to gas without passing through the liquid phase.
Conclude that the drying step in freeze-drying involves sublimation as ice turns directly into vapor.

text: Rank the following three halo-carbons in terms of increasing boiling point: 1) 1-iodopentane [one-eye-oh-doh-PEN-tane]; 2) 1-chloropentane [one kloro-PEN-tane]; 3) 1-fluoropentane [one floor-oh-PEN-tane].
explainAnswer: Identify the halogens in each compound: iodine, chlorine, and fluorine.
Recognize that boiling point increases with molecular weight and the strength of intermolecular forces.
Rank the halogens by their atomic size and polarizability: iodine > chlorine > fluorine.
Conclude that 1-iodopentane has the highest boiling point, followed by 1-chloropentane, and then 1-fluoropentane.

text: Which of the following statements is NOT true:
choices: an ideal gas cannot undergo condensation
the less mass a particle has, the faster it will effuse
when a gas is compressed, its temperature always increases
a gas is easier to compress than a liquid
explainAnswer: Identify the properties of an ideal gas and understand that it cannot undergo condensation under ideal conditions.
Recall Graham's law of effusion, which states that lighter gases effuse faster than heavier gases.
Understand that compressing a gas can lead to temperature changes, but it is not always the case that temperature increases; it depends on the process (e.g., isothermal vs. adiabatic).
Recognize that gases are generally more compressible than liquids due to the larger spaces between gas particles.

text: What is the major acidic species that forms when an acid is dissolved in water?
explainAnswer: Identify that acids release protons (H+) when dissolved in water.
Recognize that in aqueous solution, protons do not exist freely and instead associate with water molecules.
Understand that when a proton combines with a water molecule, it forms the hydronium ion (H3O+).
Conclude that the major acidic species in water is the hydronium ion.

text: Which of the following is NOT true for the reaction between silver nitrate and sodium chloride in solution?
choices: Nitrate ion is not included in the net ionic equation
Silver ion is a spectator ion
One mole of sodium nitrate is produced per mole of silver nitrate reacted
explainAnswer: Identify the reactants and products of the reaction between silver nitrate and sodium chloride.
Write the balanced molecular equation for the reaction.
Determine the ions present in the solution and identify which ones are spectator ions.
Analyze the net ionic equation to see which ions participate in the reaction and which do not.
Compare the statements given in the choices to find the one that is incorrect based on your analysis.

text: What quantum number determines if an orbital is s, p, d, or f?
explainAnswer: Identify the different types of orbitals: s, p, d, and f.
Recall that orbitals are defined by their shape and angular momentum.
Understand that the azimuthal quantum number (l) determines the shape of the orbital.
Recognize that l values correspond to specific orbitals: l=0 for s, l=1 for p, l=2 for d, and l=3 for f.

text: Which of the following statements is true regarding a gas-phase reaction at chemical equilibrium?
choices: The forward and reverse reactions stop at equilibrium
Adding reactant will increase the concentration of product
Adding reactant will increase the equilibrium constant
The reverse reaction only begins at equilibrium
explainAnswer: Understand that at chemical equilibrium, the rates of the forward and reverse reactions are equal but not the reactions themselves.
Recognize that adding more reactant shifts the equilibrium position according to Le Chatelier's principle.
Identify that this shift will favor the formation of products, thus increasing their concentration.
Eliminate the other choices based on the principles of equilibrium and reaction dynamics.

text: Identify all of the following three functional groups that commonly participate in addition reactions: 1) Aldehyde [AL-deh-hide] ; 2) Alkene ; 3) Alkyl [AL-kil] halide [HAY-lide] .
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of each functional group.
Determine which functional groups have double or triple bonds that can participate in addition reactions.
Recognize that aldehydes and alkenes both have reactive sites suitable for addition reactions, while alkyl halides do not.

text: Which of the following accurately depicts the hybridization of each atom in the molecule krypton difluoride?
explainAnswer: Identify the central atom in the molecule, which is krypton (Kr).
Determine the number of valence electrons for krypton and the fluorine atoms.
Consider the molecular geometry and the number of bonding pairs and lone pairs around the central atom.
Assign the hybridization based on the number of electron pairs around krypton, which leads to sp<sup>3</sup>d hybridization.
Recognize that each fluorine atom, with one bond and three lone pairs, has sp<sup>3</sup> hybridization.

text: Identify all of the following three compounds that have more ionic character than lithium chloride: 1) Lithium fluoride; 2) Rubidium fluoride; 3) Lithium bromide.
explainAnswer: Compare the electronegativity differences between the elements in each compound and lithium chloride.
Determine that lithium fluoride has a larger electronegativity difference than lithium chloride.
Determine that rubidium fluoride also has a larger electronegativity difference than lithium chloride.
Check lithium bromide and find that it has a smaller electronegativity difference than lithium chloride.

text: The molecular mass of atomic oxygen is expressed as 15.9994 plus or minus 0.0003. Which of the following best explains the source of the error?
choices: Human error from measurement to measurement
Lack of precision in ultra-low weighing techniques
Minute differences in measurement equipment used by different research groups
Isotopic variation in different samples of oxygen
explainAnswer: Identify the concept of isotopes and how they affect atomic mass.
Consider that atomic oxygen can exist in different isotopic forms, such as O-16, O-17, and O-18.
Recognize that variations in the abundance of these isotopes in different samples can lead to differences in measured atomic mass.
Eliminate other options by assessing their relevance to the precision of atomic mass measurements.
Conclude that isotopic variation is the most plausible source of error in the given context.

text: Rank the following three reactions in terms of increasing delta H, from most negative to most positive: 1) Combustion of one mole of formaldehyde; 2) Combustion of one mole of methanol; 3) Combustion of one mole of methane.
explainAnswer: Identify the enthalpy change (delta H) for the combustion of each substance based on their chemical structure and bond energies.
Recognize that the more carbon-hydrogen bonds a molecule has, the less negative the delta H of combustion will be.
Rank the reactions based on the number of carbon and hydrogen atoms in each molecule, with methane having the least and formaldehyde having the most.
Conclude that methane has the least negative delta H, followed by methanol, and then formaldehyde with the most negative delta H.

text: Identify all of the following three processes that would have a negative change in Gibbs free energy when conducted at atmospheric pressure: 1) Boiling of water at 95 degrees Celsius; 2) Freezing of water at 5 degrees Celsius; 3) Sublimation of ice at 105 degrees Celsius.
explainAnswer: Determine the Gibbs free energy change equation: ΔG = ΔH - TΔS.
Identify the signs of ΔH and ΔS for each process: boiling is endothermic, freezing is exothermic, and sublimation is endothermic.
Calculate ΔG for each process at the given temperatures, considering that a negative ΔG indicates a spontaneous process.
Conclude that only the sublimation of ice at 105 degrees Celsius results in a negative ΔG due to the high temperature favoring the entropy increase.

text: Which of the following molecules has a tetrahedral molecular geometry?
explainAnswer: Identify the central atom in each molecule and count the number of bonding pairs and lone pairs around it.
Determine the electron geometry based on the number of bonding and lone pairs using VSEPR theory.
For a tetrahedral geometry, there should be four bonding pairs and no lone pairs on the central atom.
Evaluate each option: Carbon tetrafluoride has four fluorine atoms bonded to carbon with no lone pairs, confirming its tetrahedral shape.
The other options either have lone pairs or a different number of bonding pairs, leading to different geometries.

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true of the kinetic theory of gases: 1) The gas molecules are constantly moving in random directions with the same speed; 2) The distances between gas molecules are much greater than the size of the molecules; 3) The collisions of molecules with the walls of the container are elastic.
explainAnswer: Review the basic principles of the kinetic theory of gases.
Identify the characteristics of gas molecules, focusing on their motion and spacing.
Evaluate each statement to determine if it aligns with the principles of the kinetic theory.
Confirm that statement 1 is false because gas molecules do not have the same speed.
Conclude that statements 2 and 3 are true based on the principles of the kinetic theory.

text: The osmotic pressure of a 0.5 molar solution of glucose is measured to be 12 atmospheres. To the nearest whole atmosphere, what is the osmotic pressure of a 2-molar solution of glucose?
explainAnswer: Identify that osmotic pressure is directly proportional to the molarity of the solution.
Use the formula for osmotic pressure: π = iCRT, where i is the van 't Hoff factor (1 for glucose), C is the molarity, R is the ideal gas constant, and T is the temperature in Kelvin.
Since the osmotic pressure is proportional to the molarity, calculate the ratio of the new molarity (2 M) to the original molarity (0.5 M).
Multiply the original osmotic pressure (12 atm) by the ratio (2 M / 0.5 M = 4) to find the new osmotic pressure.
Thus, the new osmotic pressure is 12 atm * 4 = 48 atm.

text: Identify all of the following three molecules that have an empirical formula consisting of only one type of atom: 1) Charcoal; 2) Diamond; 3) Hexane.
explainAnswer: Identify the composition of each molecule.
Charcoal is made of carbon atoms, diamond is also made of carbon atoms, and hexane is made of carbon and hydrogen atoms.
Determine if the empirical formula of each molecule consists of only one type of atom.
Charcoal and diamond both have empirical formulas of C, while hexane has an empirical formula of C6H14.
Conclude that only diamond has an empirical formula consisting of only one type of atom.

text: Which of the following molecules is NOT matched correctly to its central atom hybridization?
explainAnswer: Identify the central atom in each molecule and determine its valence electron count.
Determine the molecular geometry and the number of bonding and lone pairs around the central atom.
Assign the correct hybridization based on the number of electron groups (bonding pairs + lone pairs).
Compare the assigned hybridization with the given options to find the incorrect match.
Conclude that Phosphorous pentachloride is incorrectly matched to d2sp3 hybridization.

text: The precipitation reaction caused by the addition of potassium chloride to aqueous [AY-kwee-us] silver nitrate is an example of which of the following types of reactions?
explainAnswer: Identify the reactants involved in the reaction, which are potassium chloride and silver nitrate.
Recognize that a metathesis reaction involves the exchange of ions between two compounds.
Determine the products formed from the reaction, which will include silver chloride and potassium nitrate.
Confirm that the formation of a precipitate (silver chloride) indicates a metathesis reaction has occurred.

text: Rank the following three metals in order of increasing strength as a reducing agent: 1) Copper; 2) Zinc; 3) Lead.
explainAnswer: Identify the standard reduction potentials for each metal.
Determine the strength of each metal as a reducing agent based on its reduction potential; a lower (more negative) potential indicates a stronger reducing agent.
Rank the metals from lowest to highest reduction potential to find the order of increasing strength as reducing agents.

text: In the standard zinc dry cell, the positive electrode is primarily composed of what element?
explainAnswer: Identify the components of a standard zinc dry cell.
Determine which electrode is the positive electrode.
Recall the materials typically used in the construction of the positive electrode.
Conclude that the positive electrode is primarily made of carbon.

text: What property of concentration in chemistry is defined as moles of solute per kilograms of solvent and is useful when calculating freezing-point depression and boiling-point elevation?
explainAnswer: Identify the definitions of different concentration units in chemistry.
Understand that molality is specifically defined as moles of solute per kilogram of solvent.
Recognize that molality is used in calculations involving colligative properties like freezing-point depression and boiling-point elevation.
Differentiate molality from other concentration measures such as molarity and normality to confirm the correct answer.

text: Rank the following three substances in order of increasing melting point: 1) Sucrose; 2) Table salt; 3) Water.
explainAnswer: Identify the types of bonding in each substance: sucrose has covalent bonds, table salt has ionic bonds, and water has hydrogen bonds.
Recall that ionic compounds generally have higher melting points than covalent and hydrogen-bonded substances due to the strength of ionic interactions.
Rank the substances based on their bonding: water (hydrogen bonds) has the lowest melting point, followed by sucrose (covalent bonds), and table salt (ionic bonds) has the highest melting point.
Conclude the order of increasing melting points as water, sucrose, and table salt.

text: Which of the following atoms is commonly found in a +3 oxidation state?
explainAnswer: Identify the common oxidation states of each element in the choices provided.
Recall that Iron (Fe) commonly exhibits oxidation states of +2 and +3.
Review the other elements: Calcium typically has a +2 state, Nickel can have +2 and +3 but is less common, and Zirconium usually has +4.
Conclude that Iron is the only element in the list that is commonly found in a +3 oxidation state.

text: Andrew synthesizes a compound that consists of a benzene ring with an alcohol group in the one position and a primary amine in the four position. Identify all of the following three names that unambiguously represent the structure of this compound: 1) P-aminophenol; 2) 4-aminophenol; 3) 4-hydroxyaniline.
